design:
Clocked ledger memory for a frozen LLM (plan: obsidian/demos/proposals/2026-09-23-clocked-ledger-memory-experiment-plan.md).

Design (the spectral-native "fourth table"): an append-only ledger of records, read by exact
selection, never blended and never overwritten.

WRITE (streaming, from text alone)
  Each sentence is run through the frozen Qwen truncated at ``layer``; a small learned token
  tagger marks entity mentions (people, objects). A sentence with >= 1 mention becomes one
  record: (t = position/tick, text, keys = normalized mention strings, ttl). Keys are exact
  integer addresses (a hash index), so a lookup is O(1) and has no ties.
  The tagger trains on names, objects and verbs DISJOINT from bAbI/BABILong, so every test
  entity is held out.

READ (exact program, no learning)
  hop 1: for each key in the question, the latest m1 records with t <= T that are not expired
  hop 2: for every other key those records mention, the latest m2 records up to T and up to the
         last hop-1 record (the second key comes from the selected record itself: exact chaining)
  The selected records, in time order, are the frozen LLM's whole context. If no valid record
  exists the memory abstains ("unknown").

SHARED HELPERS (fairness rule: the baselines get the same)
  expiry: ``valid for N ticks`` is read by the same numeral regex the rag-timestamps-ttl-RULE
  baseline uses; expiry is the exact integer test (T - t) >= ttl.
